title: Cain to the Flood, part 2 of 5: the wickedness of man; Noah and the ark
style: Classical oil painting on canvas, visible expressive brushstrokes and palette-knife texture, dramatic chiaroscuro, rich earthy palette of ochre, umber, olive and deep blue. The world before the flood: wild open country, people dressed in simple garments of rough undyed wool or animal skin, tools of wood, stone and bronze, nothing man-made beyond what the scene describes. Cinematic 16:9 landscape composition. No text, no borders, no watermark, no modern objects.

NOAH.name: Noah
NOAH.desc: Noah, a strong weathered man who looks about fifty, with warm brown skin, thick grey-streaked dark hair to his collar, a full grey-streaked beard, deep-set kind eyes and a lined brow, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough undyed brown wool with a leather belt and a darker wool mantle over one shoulder, and simple leather sandals

NOAH_WIFE.name: Noah's wife
NOAH_WIFE.desc: Noah's wife, a strong, kind-faced woman who looks about forty-five, with warm brown skin, grey-streaked black hair in one long thick braid over her shoulder, dark warm eyes and laughter lines, wearing an ankle-length dress of rough undyed cream wool with a brown wool shawl around her shoulders, and simple leather sandals

SHEM.name: Shem
SHEM.desc: Shem, a son of Noah, a lean, thoughtful man of about thirty with warm brown skin, wavy black hair to his jaw and a short neat black beard, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough undyed cream wool with a rope belt, and simple leather sandals

HAM.name: Ham
HAM.desc: Ham, a son of Noah, a stocky, broad-shouldered man of about thirty with warm brown skin, close-cropped curly black hair and a thick short black beard, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough rust-brown wool with a leather belt, and simple leather sandals

JAPHETH.name: Japheth
JAPHETH.desc: Japheth, a son of Noah, a tall, rangy man of about thirty with warm brown skin, long straight black hair tied back at the nape of his neck and a thin beard along his jaw, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough dark-grey wool with a leather belt, and simple leather sandals

segs.text: Now when men began to multiply on the face of the earth and daughters were born to them,
the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and they took as wives whomever they chose.
So the LORD said,
My Spirit will not contend with man forever, for he is mortal; his days shall be 120 years.
The Nephilim were on the earth in those days—and afterward as well—when the sons of God had relations with the daughters of men.
And they bore them children who became the mighty men of old, men of renown.
Then the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great upon the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time.
And the LORD regretted that He had made man on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart.
So the LORD said,
I will blot out man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth—every man and beast and crawling creature and bird of the air—for I am grieved that I have made them.
Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD.
This is the account of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation; Noah walked with God.
And Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
Now the earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and full of violence.
And God looked upon the earth and saw that it was corrupt; for all living creatures on the earth had corrupted their ways.
Then God said to Noah,
The end of all living creatures has come before Me, because through them the earth is full of violence. Now behold, I will destroy both them and the earth.
Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; make rooms in the ark and coat it with pitch inside and out.
And this is how you are to build it: The ark is to be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
You are to make a roof for the ark, finish its walls a cubit from the top, place a door in the side of the ark, and build lower, middle, and upper decks.
And behold, I will bring floodwaters upon the earth to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life. Everything on the earth will perish.
But I will establish My covenant with you, and you will enter the ark—you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.
And you are to bring two of every living creature into the ark—male and female—to keep them alive with you.
Two of every kind of bird and animal and crawling creature will come to you to be kept alive.
You are also to take for yourself every kind of food that is eaten and gather it as food for yourselves and for the animals.
So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.

Men multiply on the face of the earth: a broad river plain seen from a hillside in morning light, crowded from the foreground to the horizon with {CAMP}, small mud-brick villages, flocks, cooking fires and hundreds of tiny people at work, smoke rising everywhere. Wide view.

Daughters were born to them: a mother in a rough wool dress seated in the doorway of a goat-hair tent holding {INFANT} girl, while her three older daughters, girls and young women in ankle-length undyed wool dresses, grind grain on a stone and spin wool beside her, smiling. Exactly five people: one woman, three girls and one baby. Medium view.

The sons of God saw: in the foreground three {SONS}, standing on a rocky ridge and looking down; far below them in the bright valley a group of young women in long undyed wool dresses draw water at a stone-ringed well, unaware. Wide view over the dark shoulders of the three watchers.

The daughters of men were beautiful: a young woman with warm brown skin, dark eyes and long black hair, in a modest long-sleeved ankle-length dress of undyed cream wool, lifting a clay water jar to her shoulder beside a stone-ringed well in golden morning light, glancing up with a bright open face; two other young women in long wool dresses fill jars behind her. Exactly three women, no men. Medium close view.

They took as wives whomever they chose: a marriage procession at dusk winding toward {CAMP}; in the foreground one of the {SONS}, leads a young bride in a long undyed wool dress and a head-covering veil by the hand; behind them two more such couples follow, while villagers stand aside watching in silence. Everyone fully clothed. Wide view from behind the procession.
The LORD speaks: {GLORY}, breaking through clouds high above a crowded plain of tents and mud-brick villages where tiny people go about their work unaware. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Very wide view.

For he is mortal: a very old man with white hair and a long white beard, in a rough wool tunic, seated alone on a stone at sunset, watching dry earth run out between the fingers of his raised hand, the low sun behind him. {ONE}. Medium close view.

The Nephilim were on the earth in those days: five powerful warriors standing in a line along the crest of a bare ridge at dusk, seen from far below as black silhouettes against a red sky, carrying long spears and hide shields, with nothing beside them to show their size. No faces visible. Wide low-angle view.

Villagers in rough wool, men and women, backing away against the mud-brick wall of a house and shielding a child, staring upward in fear at something outside the frame, while the long dark shadow of a warrior with a spear falls across the ground and up the wall beside them. The warrior himself is not in the picture, only his shadow. Medium view.

A single dark goat-hair tent at night, glowing softly from within with lamplight, its door flap closed, a man's long hooded mantle and a woman's wool shawl hanging together on the tent pole outside, under a sky of stars. {NOPEOPLE}. Medium-wide view.

They bore them children: a young mother in a long undyed wool dress seated on a fleece inside a tent, holding a sturdy {INFANT} boy on her lap, while a strong little boy of about four in a small wool tunic stands beside her brandishing a stick like a spear. Exactly one woman, one small boy and one baby. Medium view.

The mighty men of old: a towering, heavily muscled warrior with a black beard, in a rough wool kilt and a lion-skin cloak, holding a bronze-tipped spear and a round hide shield, standing with one foot on a boulder before a crowd of men who raise their arms and shout his name at sunset. No Roman or medieval armour, no metal helmet. Medium-wide low-angle view.

The LORD saw: night over a wide dark land seen from high above, dotted from end to end with the red glow of burning encampments and columns of smoke, while far above {GLORY}, looks down through a rift in the clouds. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Very wide view.

The wickedness of man was great: raiders in rough wool and hides with burning torches and wooden clubs drive off a herd of goats and cattle from an encampment of tents at night, one tent ablaze, while the people of the camp flee into the dark. {NOGORE}. No Roman or medieval armour. Wide view.

A richly fed man in a fine wool mantle, with two servants behind him, wrenches the lead rope of a single goat out of the hands of a ragged old widow who kneels in the dust before her poor hut pleading, daylight. Exactly four people. {NOGORE}. Medium view.

Every inclination of the thoughts of his heart: close view of a hard-faced bearded man seated alone by a low fire at night, half his face in deep shadow, staring across the flames with narrowed eyes while his hand slowly closes around the hilt of a bronze knife at his belt. {ONE}. Close view.
The LORD regretted: {GLORY}, now dimmed and veiled behind heavy grey cloud so that only pale muted shafts reach a silent, darkened land of scattered tents. {NOLIGHTFIG}. No rain. Very wide view.

He was grieved in His heart: a burned-out encampment at grey dawn, blackened tent poles and ashes still smoking in a silent valley, a single pale shaft of light from the clouded sky resting on a child's small clay bowl lying overturned in the ashes. {NOPEOPLE}. Medium-wide view.
The LORD speaks: {GLORY}, above {CLOUDS}, and far beneath it {TOWN}, its lanes packed with tiny people buying, selling and feasting, none of them looking up. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Very wide view.
Every man and beast: a mixed herd of wild oxen, deer and wild asses grazing on an open plain lift their heads all at once and stand uneasy, ears pricked, under {CLOUDS}. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide view.

Crawling creature and bird of the air: in the foreground a lizard and a small snake basking on a sunlit rock; beyond them a great flock of birds wheels up from a marsh into {CLOUDS}. {NOPEOPLE}. Medium-wide view.

Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD: under {CLOUDS}, a single shaft of golden light breaks through and falls on one man alone in a stony field, {NOAH}, who has stopped his work with a wooden hoe and lifts his face to the light. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Wide view.
Head-and-shoulders view of {NOAH}, his face lifted and bathed in warm golden light from above against a dark cloudy sky, his eyes open, humble and unafraid. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Close view.

A righteous man: at the edge of a dusty road {NOAH}, kneeling to pour grain from his own sack into the bowl of a ragged poor woman kneeling on the ground, while behind them other travellers walk past without looking. Medium view.

Blameless in his generation: {NOAH}, walking calmly and alone down the middle of a crowded lane in {TOWN}, while on both sides of him men brawl, gamble with knucklebones, drink from wineskins and quarrel over goods; he looks straight ahead and touches none of it. Medium-wide view.
Noah walked with God: {NOAH}, walking along a hill path at dawn with his face turned in peace toward {WALKLIGHT}. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Wide view.

The three sons of Noah working side by side to raise a new goat-hair tent in morning light: on the left {SHEM}, tying a rope to a stake; in the middle {HAM}, lifting the centre pole; on the right {JAPHETH}, drawing the cloth tight. Exactly three people in the picture, all men, no one else. Medium-wide view.

The earth was full of violence: two bands of men in rough wool and hides clash on a dusty plain with wooden clubs, bronze-tipped spears and hide shields, dust boiling up around them, a burning village behind. {NOGORE}. No Roman or medieval armour, no swords, no metal helmets. Wide view.

God looked upon the earth: a view from very high above, as if from the height of heaven, down through parted clouds lit golden from above onto a vast land of plains, rivers and hills where columns of dark smoke rise from many burning places. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {NOPEOPLE}. Very wide aerial view.

All living creatures had corrupted their ways: at dusk a ring of shouting men in rough wool goad two snarling mastiff dogs to fight each other in a dusty pen, throwing down wagers of goods, while in the background a pack of wolves scatters an untended flock of sheep. {NOGORE}. Medium-wide view.

God speaks to Noah: on a bare hilltop before dawn {NOAH}, has fallen to his knees and shields his eyes with one raised arm as {GLORY}, floods the ground in front of him. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Wide view.
Head-and-shoulders view of {NOAH}, kneeling, his face lit from above by strong golden-white light, listening with wide, stricken eyes, his lips parted. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Close view.

I will destroy both them and the earth: {NOAH}, seen from behind, kneeling bowed low toward the ground on a hilltop, golden light on his back; far below him in the valley lies {TOWN}, with smoke rising from it under a dark sky. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Wide view from behind him.

An ark of gopher wood: in a forest of tall straight cypress-like trees {NOAH}, and {HAM}, swing bronze axes with wooden hafts into the trunk of a great tree, chips flying, one felled trunk already lying beside them. {TWO_MEN}. Medium-wide view.

Make rooms in the ark: inside the lowest level of {ARKFRAME}, {SHEM}, drives a wooden peg with a wooden mallet to fix a plank wall between two of a long row of timber stalls and compartments, sunlight falling through the open beams above. {ONE}. Medium view.

Coat it with pitch inside: in the dim timber interior of the ark, {HAM}, spreads thick black pitch over the plank wall with a brush of bound reeds, dipping it in a steaming clay pot of hot pitch set over embers on a bed of stones, the coated planks gleaming black. {ONE}. Medium view.

And out: on wooden scaffolding against the towering straight outer wall of the ark, {JAPHETH}, spreads black pitch over the timbers with a brush of bound reeds, half the wall above him already gleaming black, half still pale bare wood, a clay pot of pitch beside him. {ONE}. Low-angle medium-wide view.

This is how you are to build it: {NOAH}, walking away along a very long measuring cord stretched tight between wooden stakes across level ground, a measuring rod in his hand, the cord running on and on into the far distance toward a tiny final stake. {ONE}. Wide view along the cord.

Three hundred cubits long, fifty wide, thirty high: {ARKFRAME}, seen from a hill in afternoon light, stretching across the plain, far longer than it is tall, with tiny men at work on the scaffolding, oxen dragging squared logs toward it and stacks of timber around. Very wide view.

A roof for the ark: high on top of the ark {SHEM}, and {JAPHETH}, kneel on the sloping timbers laying long roof planks side by side and pegging them down with wooden mallets, the plain far below them. {TWO_MEN}. High medium-wide view along the roof.

Finish its walls a cubit from the top: inside the upper level of the ark, {NOAH}, reaches up and measures with his forearm, from elbow to fingertips, the narrow open gap left between the top of the timber wall and the roof, daylight streaming in through the long gap above his head. {ONE}. Medium view.

A door in the side of the ark: at a great square doorway cut in the middle of the long black pitch-coated side of the ark, at the top of a broad timber ramp, {HAM}, and {JAPHETH}, heave a massive door of thick planks upright into its frame with ropes. Exactly one doorway. {TWO_MEN}. Medium-wide view.

Lower, middle and upper decks: the inside of the ark seen in cross-section by lamplight, exactly three floors of heavy timber one above another, a lower deck, a middle deck and an upper deck, joined by wooden ladders, with a man in a wool tunic at work on each of the three floors. Exactly three levels, no more. Wide interior view.

Behold, I will bring floodwaters: {NOAH}, standing on the scaffolding of the ark with a mallet lowered in his hand, looking up at an immense tower of dark storm cloud building over the plain, edged with golden light from behind. No rain yet. {ONE}. Low-angle wide view.

A foreseeing of the words: an endless expanse of dark heaving water under a black sky, great grey waves rolling from horizon to horizon in driving rain, with no land, no ark, no boat, no people and no animals anywhere. Wide view.

Everything on the earth will perish: in the foreground the people of {TOWN}, feast, drink and dance in a torchlit square at dusk, heedless; far behind them on a rise stands the ark, small in the distance: a very long, low, straight-sided rectangular black vessel like a great chest, with squared ends and a low-pitched roof, with no prow, no curved hull and no mast, under {CLOUDS}. Wide view.

I will establish My covenant with you: {NOAH}, standing upright on a hilltop with his open hands lifted a little before him, wrapped in a warm shaft of golden light that falls on him alone while the land around lies in cloud shadow. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium-wide view.

You and your sons and your wife and your sons' wives: the family of Noah seated in a circle around an evening fire outside a goat-hair tent, the long dark wall of the ark behind them. Facing us are {NOAH}, and beside him {NOAH_WIFE}; around the fire sit their three grown sons, three bearded men of about thirty in wool tunics, and the sons' three young wives in long wool dresses, some seen from behind. Exactly eight people: four men and four women, no children, no one else. Wide view.

Two of every living creature, male and female: a maned lion and a lioness standing side by side on a flat rock above the grasslands at dawn, both with heads raised, looking toward the same distant point. Exactly two animals: one male lion with a mane and one lioness. {NOPEOPLE}. Medium-wide view.

Male and female, to keep them alive: a great tusked bull elephant and a smaller cow elephant walking side by side through tall golden grass in morning light, both heading the same way. Exactly two elephants, no calves. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide view.
Two of every kind of bird: two white storks rising together on broad wings from a reed bed into a clear morning sky. Exactly two birds. {NOPEOPLE}. Medium-wide view.

And animal and crawling creature: in the foreground two tortoises crawl one behind the other across sun-warmed stones; beyond them a stag with antlers and a doe step out of a wood together, all four creatures moving in the same direction. Exactly two tortoises and two deer. {NOPEOPLE}. Medium view, low to the ground.

Every kind of food that is eaten: in front of a goat-hair tent {NOAH_WIFE}, pours golden grain from a basket into a tall clay storage jar, while beside her {WIFE_S}, and {WIFE_H}, and {WIFE_J}, fill baskets with dried figs, dates, lentils and strings of onions. Exactly four women, no men. Medium-wide view.

Food for yourselves and for the animals: {HAM}, and {JAPHETH}, carry great bundles of hay and sacks of grain on their shoulders up a broad timber ramp toward the one large open door in the long black side of the ark, more bundles of fodder stacked at the foot of the ramp. {TWO_MEN}. Medium-wide low-angle view.

Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him: the finished ark standing alone on a level plain at sunset, seen whole from the side: {ARK}. A few tiny people at the foot of the timber ramp to its door show how vast it is. Very wide view.

{NOAH}, seen from behind and to one side, standing alone at the foot of a broad timber ramp that leads up to the single open door, dark inside, in the towering black pitch-coated wall of the finished ark, while above it {CLOUDS}, spreads across the whole sky. {ONE}. Low-angle wide view.

card_notes: Every spoken word is Scripture: Genesis 6:1–22, complete.
notes: Text: Genesis 6:1-22 in full, no verses skipped or abridged. Speakers: N narrator, G the voice of God (as in s01e01a-s01e02a). Noah does not speak in this chapter.
Still tags: T = from the text, I = inferred, D = dramatized. REF = character reference sheet (not used in the film, no clip). Still 'verses' are chapter:verse.

Faces: NOAH reuses refs/REF-NOAH.jpg and the description text from s01e02a word for word; his age is not advanced (500 at 5:32, 600 at 7:6: he stays the weathered man of about fifty, I). New sheets made by this unit: refs/REF-SHEM.jpg, REF-HAM.jpg, REF-JAPHETH.jpg, REF-NOAH-WIFE.jpg. The three sons are painted as men of about thirty, the same apparent age, because their birth order is disputed; all three have the same warm brown skin as their parents and differ only in build, hair, beard and tunic colour (cream, rust-brown, dark grey). Noah's wife and the sons' wives are unnamed in the text; the sons' wives have description blocks only (WIFE_S, WIFE_H, WIFE_J, each dressed in her husband's colour). Genesis 7-9 units must reuse all of these word for word.

The sons of God (6:2, 6:4): who they were is disputed (angelic beings, the line of Seth, or rulers). Not resolved: they are tall mantled men seen only from behind, backlit, faces never visible, with no wings, halos or crowns (block SONS), so no reading is ruled in or out. 'Took as wives' is a marriage procession; 'had relations' (6:4) is implied only by a closed lamplit tent (D3), nothing shown.

The Nephilim (6:4): the text here does not describe them or say whose children they were. They are black silhouettes of warriors on a ridge with nothing beside them to give scale (D1) and a warrior's long shadow (D2, D), so their size is neither asserted nor denied. The 'mighty men of old, men of renown' are a warrior acclaimed by a crowd (D5).
6:3: '120 years' is disputed (a shortened lifespan or the time left before the flood); the picture shows only mortality (an old man, dust running through his fingers) and takes no side.

God is light only (GLORY), never a figure. His seeing (6:5, 6:12) is a view from above; His regret and grief (6:6) are the light veiled by cloud and one pale shaft on a burned camp (F1, F2 D). No rain falls anywhere in this unit.

Wickedness and violence (6:5, 6:11-13): the text gives no particulars. Raids, robbery of a widow, brooding malice, a battle and a dog-fight are illustrations (T for the fact, particulars D), all without wounds or blood. 'All living creatures had corrupted their ways' (6:12) is shown with men and beasts both (L2).
Noah's righteousness (6:9): giving grain to a widow (I1) is D. 'Walked with God' repeats the picture used for Enoch in s01e02a (WALKLIGHT), since the text uses the same words of both.

The ark (6:14-16): painted as the text measures it, a long straight-sided chest 300 by 50 by 30 cubits (ten times as long as high), not a ship with a prow (blocks ARK and ARKFRAME; later units must reuse ARK word for word). 'Gopher wood' is of unknown kind: tall cypress-like trees (I). 'Finish its walls a cubit from the top' is read as an opening one cubit high under the roof all round (I; the Hebrew is disputed). One door in the long side, with a timber ramp (I). Three decks (P4). Tools are bronze axes, adzes, mallets and pegs (I, from 4:22).

Order of events: the pictures under 6:14-16 and 6:21 show Noah and his sons carrying out each command as it is spoken; the text reports the obedience once, in 6:22. This compresses time and is D. No animals are shown coming to the ark in this unit: that is told in Genesis 7. The animals under 6:19-20 are pairs in the wild (male and female where the kinds differ visibly). Q2, the waters, is a foreseeing of God's words in 6:17 and is D; nothing in this unit shows the flood as having begun.
R2 shows the eight named in 6:18 (Noah, his wife, three sons, three sons' wives). W2, Noah before the open door under gathering cloud, is D and hands over to Genesis 7.
Narration is not generated in this unit; shots are laid at assembly.
